statements.statement: Taylor Zundel posted a video on Instagram on October 26, 2020, claiming that she and her husband were told they had already voted when they went to early voting in Salt Lake County, Utah, suggesting that multiple people experienced this issue within a short timeframe.
statements.support_span: The controversy started when a woman posted a video on the Instagram account for Taylor Zundel on October 26, 2020 in which she relayed what happened when she and her husband went to early voting that day in Salt Lake County, Utah. | This happened to TWO different people within the short 5-10 mins I was voting. This isn't okay! Spread the word.

statements.statement: The incident where voters were told they had already voted was due to a technical error by a poll worker, not widespread fraud, occurring because a poll worker failed to electronically clear the voter access card, causing the machine to display an incorrect message; Salt Lake County Clerk Sherry Swensen confirmed that official records showed the affected voters had not actually voted previously and that the issue was limited to a small number of people and was not a systematic denial of voting rights.
statements.support_span: But it happened to only a few people and was due to a technical error by a poll worker. silver.justification: The evidence confirms that Taylor Zundel did post an Instagram video on October 26, 2020, claiming that she and her husband, along with others, were told they had already voted while attempting to vote early in Salt Lake County, Utah. However, the evidence clarifies that this was not a systematic denial of voting rights, but rather a technical error caused by a poll worker failing to properly clear voter access cards, which triggered an incorrect error message on the machines. Salt Lake County Clerk Sherry Swensen confirmed that official records showed the affected individuals had not actually voted previously and that the issue was limited to a small number of people.
